title: Introduce CI shard health-checker + dependency-janitor cron; refactor lint/test orchestration
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add CI shard health checker that detects long-tail flaky shards and rebalances jobs; introduce dependency-janitor scheduled workflow that creates safe update PRs for low-risk transitive deps; refactor lint/test orchestration to share lightweight launcher and reduce matrix duplication.
description:
Motivation: Over the last quarter we observed increased CI flakiness concentrated in a small number of GitHub Actions shards (slow runners, env misconfiguration, or transient network spikes). Separately, our dependency update cadence has become noisy: Renovate/Open-source bots create many PRs for low-risk transitive bumps that don't require human attention. This PR introduces two production-safe automation pieces and a small refactor to the existing lint/test orchestration to reduce noise and improve CI stability.

What this PR does (single-string description):
- CI shard health-checker (tools/ci/shard_health.py + .github/workflows/ci-health-check.yml): periodic job (every 3h) that aggregates shard runtimes from workflow run artifacts and checks for long-tail failure/retry patterns. It annotates failing workflows, opens an internal issue when a shard crosses predefined thresholds (median runtime > X, failure rate > Y), and can mark a shard as quarantined to avoid scheduling future matrix jobs there for 24h. The health-checker emits metrics (Prometheus pushgateway via internal endpoint) and writes a compact status.json artifact so downstream orchestration can prefer healthier shards.
- Dependency-janitor (scripts/dep_janitor.py + .github/workflows/dep-janitor.yml): weekly scheduled workflow that scans package manifests (go.mod, package.json, pyproject.toml) for low-risk transitive updates (patch releases, semver-safe). For candidates, the janitor creates a single rollup PR per package-ecosystem containing grouped changelogs, test matrix outcomes from a dry-run job, and a suggested merge window label (e.g., "maintenance/low-risk"). The job uses a guarded approach: only PRs that pass our lightweight smoke tests and have no incompatible transitive changes are opened. Overrides are available via repo config (ci/dep-janitor-config.yaml).
- Lint/test orchestration refactor: extracted a small launcher (scripts/ci/runner_launcher.sh) which normalizes environment variables, sets up tool cache, and reuses a single lint job across subpackages to reduce matrix duplication. This reduces redundant setup time and reduced average CI minutes for lint runs by ~18% in our internal benchmark.

Design notes and safety:
- The shard health-checker runs in audit-only mode by default for the first week after rollout (we do not quarantine shards or open issues automatically). It emits detailed logs to the workflow run and an artifact with historical bucketed runtimes. After one week, the job will be flipped to active (a release flag flip in infra-config).
- The dependency-janitor explicitly filters out direct dependency major bumps and any packages in the "do-not-janitor" list. PRs created include an automated label and a required reviewer from the owning team. By default it targets the "dev" branch, not main, so merges are gated behind normal review policies.
- All new scripts are written with idempotency and small memory footprint; Python code pins only runtime deps and vendors a small helper library to avoid transient network fetches during the workflow.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Local unit tests added for shard scoring algorithm (tests/test_shard_health.py) and dep-janitor candidate selection (tests/test_dep_janitor.py).
- Staged rollout: first enable workflows in the redwood/infra and redwood/helm repos for 48h in audit-only mode; then opt-in the rest of core repo.
- Observability: dashboards added (dashboards/ci-shard-health.json) with run-rate, median/95th runtime per shard, quarantined shards, and janitor-created PR delta. Alerts created for sustained median > 2x baseline.

Checklist (what I did):
- [x] Implement shard health-checker script and workflow
- [x] Implement dependency-janitor script and scheduled workflow
- [x] Refactor lint/test runner launcher and simplify matrix configs
- [x] Add unit tests and smoke workflow for new jobs
- [x] Add dashboard and alert rules for visibility
- [x] Update CONTRIBUTING.md and internal runbook for janitor behavior

What I did NOT change: release automation pipelines, deploy hooks, or any customer-facing release steps. The changes are scoped to CI, repo maintenance automation, and observability.

Related work: ENG-1428 (CI stability initiative), ENG-2103 (repo hygiene roadmap), SUP-88 (support ticket that surfaced dependency noise).

Notes for reviewers: focus review on the shard scoring heuristics (shard_health.py) and the safety gates in dep_janitor.py. The lint/test refactor is intentionally small (move + small wrapper) to minimize merge conflict surface.

reviews: Jonah Kim (requested changes): Can we reduce permissions scope for the janitor bot? Suggested: use checkout-with-token and fine-grained token with repo:status and pull_request scope only.
Aisha Patel (response): Updated janitor to use fine-grained token; added fallback branch protection check to avoid accidental direct merges.
Mariela Costa (approved): Verified shard scoring tests and smoke run on infra repo; logging is sufficient for audit-mode.
Evan Brooks (comment): Consider adding a small canary that targets low-risk packages for the first 2 weeks. (Followed-up by janitor config change)
Aisha Patel (reply): Added canary flag and updated ci/dep-janitor-config.yaml to default to canary=true for first 2 runs.
